newsitem.title: CANADA: One of four IPL crude lines reopened after spill.
newsitem.headline: One of four IPL crude lines reopened after spill.

text.p: IPL Energy Inc said Friday that it closed four lines on its Interprovincial pipeline system after a local Manitoba resident reported an oil smell, though one has recently been restarted and the others are expected back up shortly.
"Lines one, 2b, three and 13 were shut down this morning at (0630) Manitoba time upon report of a crude oil smell reported by a local resident," said Alan Roth, spokesman for IPL.

"Since then, we've had reports that it is a small spill -- 30 cubic meters which is about 180/190 barrels -- and line one has been restarted. It is a minor spill and the lines might be restarted shortly but we are waiting to find out which line is the source of the spill," Roth added.
He said it would be too early to estimate how much of IPL's daily throughput might be lost.

Interprovincial combines with the Lakehead system on the U.S. side of the border and the system, running from Edmonton, Alberta through Superior, Wis. and Chicago to various points in southern Ontario, is the world's longest crude oil and liquids pipeline complex.

IPL lost throughput for several days earlier this month after bad weather in Minnesota knocked out three pumping stations. The throughput prior to that incident was 1.4 million barrels and the outage cut half Canada's oil movement temporarily.
